title: Crypto Cycles
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/0/body: Every **210,000 blocks** (roughly every **4 years**), Bitcoin's **block reward** gets **cut in half**, so new bitcoin is created half as fast. This rule has been in Bitcoin's code since day one, and it's what keeps supply under **21 million**.
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/1/prompt: After the 2024 halving, each block's reward is 3.125 BTC. What will it be after the next halving (around 2028)?
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/1/explanatio: A halving means cutting in half: 3.125 ÷ 2 = 1.5625 BTC. 0.78 is what you'd get two halvings from now.
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/2/statement: The halving happens exactly every 4 calendar years, on a fixed date.
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/2/explanatio: The halving depends on the block count (every 210,000 blocks), not the calendar. Since blocks don't come exactly every 10 minutes, the date shifts a little each time.
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/3/body: With each halving, **new daily supply is cut in half**: after 2024, it's about **450 BTC a day** (144 blocks × 3.125). That means miners have less bitcoin to sell each day, and Bitcoin's yearly inflation has dropped to **under 1%**.
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/4/prompt: This is a made-up monthly Bitcoin chart, and the halving happened on the marked candle. Which common pattern from past cycles does it show?
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/4/options/0/: A strong rise in the months after, then a pullback
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/4/options/1/: A big drop in the halving month itself
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/4/options/3/: The price top exactly on halving day
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/4/explanatio: Price ranged around the halving, topped out about 14 months later, then pulled back. In past cycles, tops usually came 12 to 18 months after the halving, but that's a pattern, not a law.
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/5/pairs/0/me: The block reward getting cut in half
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/5/pairs/2/me: Fresh bitcoin for each block's miner
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/6/body: There have only been **four halvings** so far, and other factors like **interest rates, global liquidity and institutional money** have moved price too. Many analysts believe the halving's effect is **fading**, since the share of new supply gets smaller each time and the market already sees it coming.
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/7/prompt: What challenge do miners face after a halving?
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/7/options/0: Their bitcoin income per block is cut in half, squeezing less efficient miners
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/7/options/2: They stop earning any transaction fees
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/7/options/3: They're forced to switch to Proof of Stake
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/7/explanatio: Electricity and hardware costs stay the same, but the reward is halved. If price doesn't make up for it, high-cost miners may shut down their machines or sell more bitcoin.
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/8/prompt: An influencer says: "The halving is near; price is 100% guaranteed to triple." What's the best response?
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/8/options/0: The past pattern has only 4 examples; nothing's guaranteed, so manage your risk
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/8/options/1: True; the halving always triples the price exactly
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/8/options/2: True; so you'd better buy with high leverage
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/8/options/3: The opposite; the halving always cuts the price in half
lessons/onchain-u3-l1/steps/8/explanatio: Four examples are far too few for a "guarantee", and every cycle's big-picture conditions are different. Be suspicious of anyone in the market who talks about guaranteed profit.
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/0/title: The four phases of a cycle
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/0/body: Markets usually rotate through four phases: **accumulation** (after a big drop; ranging and quiet), **markup**, **distribution** (near the top; big swings and smart money selling) and **markdown**. In crypto, these cycles tend to be very **extreme**.
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/1/prompt: Put the market cycle phases in order (starting after a big drop).
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/1/explanatio: After a drop, patient buyers accumulate; then an uptrend starts; near the top comes gradual selling (distribution); and finally the drop (markdown). Then the cycle repeats.
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/2/prompt: Price has ranged below 23,500 in an accumulation phase for a long time. Tap the candle that signaled the start of markup by closing above the top of the range.
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/2/explanatio: The earlier candles only got close to 23,500 from below. This candle closed above the top of the range with a long body and almost three times the volume, a common sign of breaking out of accumulation.
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/3/body: A pattern many people saw in past cycles: money flows into **Bitcoin** first, then **Ethereum**, then large-cap altcoins, and finally **small alts**. The period when most alts outperform Bitcoin is called **altseason**, and it usually comes with **falling Bitcoin dominance**.
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/4/prompt: Which combination fits best with the start of altseason?
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/4/options/0: Bitcoin dominance falling and ETH/BTC rising
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/4/options/1: Bitcoin dominance rising and ETH/BTC falling
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/4/options/2: Every coin dropping at once on high volume
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/4/options/3: Flat dominance and a market with no volume
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/4/explanatio: Altseason means alts grow faster than Bitcoin, so Bitcoin's share shrinks, and Ethereum, which usually leads the alts, gets stronger against Bitcoin.
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/5/statement: By one common definition, the market is in "altseason" when about 75% of the top 50 coins outperform Bitcoin over 90 days.
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/5/explanatio: That's the definition behind the "Altcoin Season Index" that many people follow. There's no single official definition, but the idea is always that most alts beat Bitcoin.
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/6/prompt: An altcoin fell 90% from its peak during a bear market. How much does it need to rise to get back to that peak?
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/6/explanatio: Going from $1 to $10 is 10x, which is a 900% gain. That's why protecting your capital in the markdown phase matters so much; many alts never return to their old peak.
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/7/pairs/0/me: Quiet range after a big drop
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/8/prompt: Bitcoin just hit a new high, its dominance is falling, small alts are pumping 50% a day, and everyone's talking about "getting rich quick". Based on cycle patterns, where are we probably in the cycle?
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/8/options/0: Late markup, close to distribution; time to be careful
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/8/options/1: Early accumulation; the best time to take more risk
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/8/options/3: There's no sign of any cycle phase
lessons/onchain-u3-l2/steps/8/explanatio: Small alts pumping and public hype usually belong to the last stages of a rally. Nobody knows exactly when the top comes, but this is a time to cut risk, not add to it.
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/0/body: In crypto, money chases **stories**, like **AI, Layer 2s, memecoins or tokenized real-world assets (RWA)**. When a narrative gets hot, almost every token in that category pumps together, even low-quality projects.
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/1/body: Hype usually follows this path: **first news** → quiet buying by smart money → **media and influencers** → **public FOMO** and the peak → a sharp crash. Most people get in after the price has **already multiplied**.
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/1/tip: As the famous saying goes: "Buy the rumor, sell the news."
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/2/prompt: Put the usual stages of a narrative's hype cycle in order.
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/2/items/4: A sharp crash after the peak
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/2/explanatio: Smart money gets in early and quietly, and by the time the media and the public arrive, it's slowly selling. The later you show up, the bigger your risk.
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/3/prompt: Tap the blow-off top candle: where the last buyers piled in on the highest volume and price got rejected.
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/3/explanatio: After several green candles, each bigger than the last, this candle has the highest volume on the chart. It reached 1.95 but closed near 1.66; the long upper wick means sellers unloaded onto the late buyers.
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/4/statement: When a narrative gets hot, the weak projects in that category usually pump along with the rest.
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/4/explanatio: Hype money looks at the category name, not project quality. And those weak projects usually drop harder than the rest after the peak.
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/5/prompt: A network upgrade everyone has waited months for happened today, and price has climbed steadily up to today. Today's candle has a long upper wick. What's the more likely next move?
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/5/explanatio: News everyone was waiting for is already priced in. On the day itself, many traders "sell the news", and the long upper wick shows sellers stepping in. A pullback is more likely, but not certain.
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/6/body: Before you get in, ask: **Does this narrative have real use, or is it just a story?** How late am I? Most importantly, set your **size and stop loss** in advance, keep hype trades **small**, and don't decide out of fear of missing out (**FOMO**).
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/7/pairs/0/me: A story that pulls money into a category
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/7/pairs/1/me: Panic that you'll miss the rally
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/7/pairs/2/me: High-volume peak with a sharp reversal
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/7/pairs/3/me: Selling as the expected news arrives
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/8/prompt: Your friend wants to buy a hot token right now with all their savings. Given these signs, what's the best advice?
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/8/facts/2/va: Even non-traders are talking about it
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/8/options/0: Lots of peak-hype signs; if they get in at all, small size and a stop loss
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/8/options/1: Jump in fast with leverage so they don't miss the train
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/8/options/2: Put in all their savings because everyone's buying
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/8/options/3: Wait until it's 10x, then buy with all their money
lessons/onchain-u3-l3/steps/8/explanatio: A sharp rise, hype everywhere and non-professionals piling in are classic signs of hype's final stages. Nobody knows exactly where the top is, so a small position size and a stop loss are your most important protection.
